# Dev

Invocation: `kc-dev-flow-2:dev`

Package root: /Users/kent/conductor/workspaces/kc-claude-plugins/colombo/.context/dev2-adoption/worktree/.worktrees/spacedock-ensign-model-roster-per-repo/kc-dev-flow-2
`<package>` in this skill and its linked files is this root. If the value above
is not an absolute path, the root is two directories above this `SKILL.md`.

Read the [framework](../../README.md). This is a start/resume entry, not a worker
stage or a second workflow controller. Claude's packaged command is
`/kc-dev-flow-2:dev`; bare `/dev` is not a promised cross-host alias.

Resolve the absolute project root, explicit workflow directory and intended work
item from the request and authoritative project/task records. Reuse established
context; do not guess between projects or tasks. Read applicable project
conventions and the existing context needed for the requested work.

After resolving the code root, run `python3 <package>/scripts/learning.py --repo
<absolute-code-root> notices --all`. Present relevant unread learning results (items
with `unread` true) to the user, distinguishing pending/uncertain, no-change, local proposal, PR and observed
merge; pending proposals are not active rules. Only after actual presentation,
run `ack --job <job> --expected <notice_digest>` for each shown snapshot. Context
injection or reading alone is not presentation. A changed digest stays unread;
interruption may repeat a notice. Settle every delivery shown `open`, acknowledged or not, by reading its PR
with `gh pr view` as learn's `Follow the delivery to a recorded end` says, before presenting.
Read failure holds that learning action, not
unrelated approved development. This entry-level check is not a host SessionStart
hook. Use [learn](../learn/SKILL.md) for an explicitly requested named-task loop;
notices do not authorize evaluation, delivery, retry or merge.

For existing work, preserve its recorded variant/profile, approved outcome,
scope, non-goals and stop condition. Read current state, reports and delivery
status instead of assuming a prior conversation is current. An invalid profile,
conflicting records or missing authority holds the dependent action; return only
the unresolved decision to the user. Do not restart approved design or ask again
for an unchanged selection.

For new work without a profile selection, establish the intended outcome and
recommend a profile using the framework's intended use and applicable shared
profile principles. Ask the user to select it before profile-dependent work.
An explicit valid selection is sufficient; FO records it with the variant in
the work item through the existing workflow. Recommendation is not selection.
For new work that adds a capability no journey map holds, ask once, before recommending a profile, whether to draw a story map first with kc-journey-map (`map`, `plan-release`, then `review-release`, which interrogates the release before splitting it). Record the result on each task as the workflow's `Release review:` line, or `Release review: not needed: <his words>`.

Hand the resolved project root, explicit workflow directory, work item, approved
selection/scope and bounded outcome to `spacedock:first-officer`, with this
skill's `Package root:` value, which FO writes into the scope notes of every
worker dispatch and follow-up message with a line telling the worker to send its completion
message to `main`, because the completion block Spacedock appends names `team-lead`. Retain that
workflow directory as `--workflow-dir` on SD commands; cwd alone is not the
binding. If FO is already active, continue there. SD owns stage selection, live
worker availability, dispatch, reports, gates and recovery; a resumed FO does
not establish that its old worker still exists. An entity sitting in a stage
declared `gate: true` is excluded from `spacedock status --next` and from
`--boot`'s DISPATCHABLE table before the concurrency check runs (Spacedock
v0.27.0, `internal/status/format.go`, `dispatchAnalysis`, reason `gate`), so an
empty dispatchable view does not mean no worker is available; three of this
workflow's five stages (`backlog`, `ideation`, `validation`) declare `gate: true`,
so that empty view is this workflow's normal case, not the exception. Stage
skills own profile routing and load the selected references in each worker's
context.

Before each worker dispatch and on resume, run `python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py
<workflow-dir>/README.md`. Exit 1 means the README FO follows differs from the trunk's,
exit 2 that it could not be compared; hold the dispatch, show the Captain the printed
remedy or cause, and wait. Do not run the remedy or move the checkout yourself. This
sentence sits here because a README old enough to be wrong may not contain it.

If adoption is absent or the selected profile does not match the ordered stage
graph, follow the [SD adoption reference](../../references/sd/adoption.md) through
`spacedock:commission` or `spacedock:refit` before dispatch. Invoking this entry does
not migrate an old variant, rewrite a workflow or install a package. Keep existing
work on its recorded variant unless a migration is explicitly approved. This
entry grants no new repair, approval, delivery or route-exception authority.

# Development workflow
<!-- kc-dev-flow-2 0.33.1 x-release-please-version -->

This is the adopted workflow's authority for SD stages and task schema. Resolve
its absolute directory and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands, including
worker reads and recovery. Skills guide work; SD owns dispatch, gates and state.

## File Naming

Each task is a flat `<slug>.md` file in the resolved state checkout. Keep existing
IDs and tasks in their recorded workflow; new work does not migrate old work.

## Schema

Record `title`, `status`, `variant: kc-dev-flow-2`, and the user's selected
`profile`; `id` is optional under `id-style: slug`. The five-stage route accepts
`pilot` or `prod`; the POC adaptation
removes ideation from both frontmatter and Stages and accepts `poc` only.
Before admission and dispatch, FO holds unknown/mismatched profiles;
SD does not enforce this rule. Preserve approved outcome and scope.
New seeds require non-empty `Non-goals:`, `Budget:` and `Stop condition:` lines
under `## Scope` or matching level-two sections. Replay counts do not enforce
these on existing tasks. Use bold **AC-N** declarations with individual evidence clauses.

## Batch gates

A Captain-approved batch covers one release slice or theme. Recover members from accepted scopes/questions, without another list. Unclear membership holds presentation; membership changes or splits need his decision. Incompatible stage graphs need an explicitly approved split.

At each next gate, wait for every member's sufficient committed evidence, then present the batch in one sitting. Early finishers prompt no decision. Continue authorized repairs/validation. A blocker needing Captain authority gets one exception question naming the member and effect. Do not manufacture hold resolutions.

`<package>/scripts/pr_watch.py tasks` sitting hints remain subject to this boundary; stage alone joins neither unrelated tasks nor incomplete batches. Unbatched tasks retain ordinary gates.

When requested, chief-engineer reviews the complete package/process batch before briefing bindings; engineering-reviewer handles contested hard-to-reverse claims. Give committed task files/artifact links, not FO's suspicions/conclusions. Record reviewer/model/evidence; use a different family from all workers or ask the Captain. Review advises, without approval authority.

## Stages

Stage workers follow `<package>/references/model-roster.md`; absence retains README defaults.
`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
a cheaper one. Record chief-engineer and engineering-reviewer calls under `## FO alignment` as
`Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`; `<package>/scripts/role_triggers.py` lists calls owed.

`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.

FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (for validation a
`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so
the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it; FO runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` before committing and fixes each part it lists. A follow-up
message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, with the same check and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
After each worker report, before advancing or preparing its gate, FO runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --coverage <task> --stage <stage>`; nonzero holds that task.
This check does not observe unrecorded messages.
Before `dispatch build`, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names --strict <record>` on the saved record; nonzero holds dispatch. Relative script paths are allowed; bare package script names remain errors. Plain `--names` preserves existing historical verdicts and reports skipped context checks on stderr. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker with the request to append a complete new report under the same heading, ending in a Summary that supersedes the earlier one, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself
does not say why; other causes are a missing evidence line or Summary and an uncommitted
report.

### `backlog`

The user selects the compatible profile and approves outcome, scope and budget.
FO records the choice; this boundary has no worker or placeholder report. FO
also records, under a `## FO alignment` heading in the task file, whether FO
direction alignment with the Captain is needed before the next declared stage
and why; a
stated reason is the whole record when not needed. On the five-stage route, FO
also records a `Surfaces:` line under the same heading: any of `ui`, `db`,
or `none`, read from the change surface rather than the diff, and next to it
a `Visible change:` line: one sentence on what a user sees or operates
differently, or `Visible change: none`.

- **Gate content:** Show the selected variant/profile, proposed outcome, scope,
  exclusions and evidence needed before the next declared stage starts, the
  `## FO alignment` need and reason, and the recorded `Surfaces:` and
  `Visible change:` lines on the five-stage route.
- **Seed check:** On the five-stage route, before `gate prepare`, FO runs
  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed <task>` and holds the
  gate until it exits 0. An FO that skips this step still dispatches; no runtime hook blocks it.
- **Release review:** Applies to a task that belongs to a release on a journey map
  (`journey`, `journey-release`, `journey-story`); a task with no release, such as a
  bug, infrastructure or workflow maintenance, is outside it. Four signals: (1) a task
  admitted into a release; (2) a Captain scope ruling that moves a story or task into
  or out of a release or changes the goal of the release, a story or a task; (3) a UAT
  failure that crosses two or more tasks; (4) a batch about to enter implementation. Signals 1 and 2 only mark the
  release changed: FO names the release and the signal in the task's `## FO alignment`
  reason. A task whose `journey-story` is already on the map in that release passes with
  that one check and marks nothing when, since its latest `Release review:` line, the
  journey file still holds the same story ids and the same release and story `goal`
  text and no Captain ruling has changed the goal of the release, a story or a task.
  A changed goal is signal 2 although no story id moved; FO marks the release
  changed in that task's `## FO alignment` reason. Signal 4 is the single checkpoint: at the first
  implementation dispatch for a release marked changed, FO dispatches a fresh worker
  with kc-journey-map's `review-release` mode, then splits tasks from its output; an
  unchanged release proceeds. One review covers every change since the last. Signal 3
  runs the review at once. FO writes no map and no candidate; the Captain accepts
  membership in conversation or at this gate. FO records under `## FO alignment` either
  `Release review: <journey>/<release-id> at <journey-file commit>` or
  `Release review: not needed: <reason>`. When FO approves
  a task into a release story at this gate it sets the three fields with
  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey=<the map's journey: value> journey-release=<id> journey-story=<id>`;
  a worker never edits frontmatter. Where the adopter tracks completion with
  kc-journey-progress, FO also writes `journey-required-tasks` (full task ids) and
  `journey-mapping-complete: true` on one task per story at the review's split step.
  When signal 2 moves a task out of a release, FO clears its release fields with
  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey= journey-release= journey-story= journey-required-tasks= journey-mapping-complete=`
  (a field set to nothing is cleared). Where kc-journey-progress is tracking, follow its
  skill for the lists; when the cleared task was the declaring one, FO moves that list and
  `journey-mapping-complete: true` to another member of the story. kc-journey-progress
  reports a story unverified until its declaration matches its members.

### `ideation`

FO may dispatch ideation on a stronger model when the design is hard to reverse,
such as an event model, an architecture or a security boundary, and says so in
the dispatch. The default ensign invokes `kc-dev-flow-2:ideation` before useful work, using the
work item's recorded variant/profile and the skill's own profile routing table.
FO aligns direction and requests research when it can change a decision; the
worker authors the PRFAQ and the artifact each recorded surface owes. When
`## FO alignment` records alignment as needed, FO records the alignment result
as a `Result:` line before dispatching the worker. Missing skill or profile
authority requires a hold report rather than a baseline or default-profile
substitution.
Ideation writes no repository file, branch or commit: the design, the criteria and any
ADR draft live in the task file, and a draft carries no ADR number.

- **Outputs:** Current design definition and acceptance criteria with reproducible
  evidence clauses; unresolved decisions identified for the user.
- **Gate content:** Present PRFAQ/Mermaid with matching actors, order, branches,
  approvals and stops, acceptance evidence/limits, and each recorded
  `Surfaces:` value's artifact. The gate is not presentable without the
  artifact each recorded surface owes. Before `spacedock gate prepare`, FO runs
  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, includes its
  output in the gate material at any exit, and treats a non-zero exit as the gate
  not presentable. Required diagram defects or missing current-stage
  evidence block recommendation and gate preparation/presentation; honest
  unverified future checks do not.
  FO may correct design prose/Mermaid to reflect established decisions under an
  actual Captain grant covering that task's exact design section; reuse a matching
  standing grant. Template adoption grants no authority. Record the decision basis;
  preserve scope, acceptance criteria, risk acceptance, product code, worker
  evidence, prior reports, approvals and verdicts. Withdraw an affected open binding
  before editing, then reprepare through the applicable SD lifecycle. Other
  corrections require an authorized author; hold where no supported route applies,
  without inventing same-stage rework. Corrections neither replace user approval nor advance stages.

### `implementation`

The default ensign invokes `kc-dev-flow-2:implementation` before useful work,
using the recorded profile and approved scope. Produce the bounded integrated
result and its evidence. Missing inputs require a hold; scope/profile changes
return to the affected user decision. Apply Review-finding disposition to repairs;
a repair is dispatched under the lane in Stages.

- **Outputs:** Exact delivered artifact, checks actually run, and material limits
  recorded in the existing SD Stage Report.

### `validation`

A fresh ensign invokes `kc-dev-flow-2:validation` before useful work and checks
the exact artifact against the accepted profile outcome. It assesses the work;
it does not silently take over implementation. Rejection uses the supported
feedback path after the distinct FO disposition described below. Its recheck of a
repair is dispatched under the lane in Stages.

- **Outputs:** Independent verdict, primary evidence, a minimal acceptance script, the
  `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>` command run with its exit
  code, and unverified obligations recorded in the existing SD Stage Report.
- **Gate content:** Show actual checks and acceptance evidence, material findings
  and limits, and the user's pending delivery decision. For a `ui` task FO runs
  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>` and includes its
  output. Before the gate, FO runs the
  stage's minimal acceptance script exactly as written in a fresh shell, then presents
  every step in full beside its observed output, never a pointer or a shortened step.
  A step FO cannot run (a secret, a sign-in, the Captain's own device) is marked not
  run with the reason; an output that differs from the script returns through feedback.
  Before recommending delivery, FO confirms both goal sufficiency and minimal
  necessity from the same candidate's existing route evidence. Passing checks or
  approval replace neither condition; approval is not merge. When a POC report
  records `boundary-crossed:`, FO shows the marker and its evidence with the
  user's choice between profile selection and removing the crossing work with
  recorded cleanup through the feedback route, and does not recommend
  delivering that work as POC.

### `done`

Consuming a terminal gate approval is not completion (`spacedock merge guard --help`);
a live run requires the declared delivery evidence and successful `merge guard` with
an explicit verdict. Apply Delivery authority below; a pending PR or missing hook is
not completion.

## Dispatch facts

- **Team:** You are one worker in a team completing the project goal; your stage
  and handoff serve that goal. Before substantial work or retrying a failure,
  check this task's prior reports, linked sibling tasks and PRs, and relevant
  workflow state: did someone already do this, hit this, or own it now? If your
  environment cannot run a required checklist check, tell FO before building
  work that depends on it. Ask FO early about overlapping ownership, repeated
  failures, missing authority or evidence, or infeasible targets. Give checked
  sources, findings, attempts and the specific question. With a mid-run FO
  channel, pause dependent work and continue safe independent work; without
  one, end your turn with that handback instead of waiting. Never answer your
  own or your reviewers' permission requests; route them to FO. FO coordinates
  peers and decisions; do not message peers or change others' work.
- **Signal:** send the completion message once, to the first officer by the name
  your session lists as addressable (`main` under Claude Code dispatch). The
  completion block's `team-lead` is Spacedock's default and is not registered
  there (spacedock-dev/spacedock #523, #608); do not try it first and do not
  describe a fallback in the report.
- **Package:** `<package>` in stage text is the `Package root:` line of the
  kc-dev-flow-2 skill you loaded; your dispatch's scope notes state the same path,
  and if they differ, use the skill's. Run package scripts only from it; never
  search the filesystem, `/tmp` or another install for them.
- **Secrets:** `<wrapper>` is the only route to a development secret: run a
  command that needs one as `<wrapper> <command>`. Never read or print a value.
  If a guard refuses a command that only mentions a secret-reading tool, rephrase
  it; do not split, encode or wrap the command to pass the guard.

## Review-finding disposition

Before repair authorization, product bytes and the recorded candidate revision stay
unchanged. Read-only inspection, non-mutating reproductions, existing tests and
throwaway-checkout probes are allowed. Report/gate commits may advance repository
HEAD without changing the candidate. Validators recommend `PASSED` or `REJECTED`;
new findings or changed evidence re-enter this checkpoint.

The four evidence fields are released user and normal workflow; observable harm;
affected value acceptance criterion or non-negotiable boundary; and trigger
evidence. Field 3 uses `value-ac[AC-N]`, `captain-ruling[YYYY-MM-DD]`, or
`contract[repo/relative/path#anchor]` plus a nonblank claim. `none:` with a rationale
does not establish Material.

- **Material:** all four fields establish supported-workflow harm to a protected
  boundary or value acceptance criterion.
- **Deferred risk:** hypothetical, unsupported, unobserved or unpromised trigger;
  record what would make it material.
- **Polish:** no current user-visible loss or protected boundary is at risk.
- **Needs decision:** the task cannot own the scope, product or compatibility call.

A `Follow-up:` line in Scope is not accepted scope by itself: the first stage of the
receiving task to meet it assesses it against its stated reason and earlier rulings. It builds the line only when the change alters no behaviour that an
accepted criterion, a Captain ruling or a journey contract relies on; otherwise it
returns the line to FO as a Needs decision. It records which, and why.
A finding FO declined in a committed gate summary or under `### FO declines` is settled:
a later validator does not report it again unless the candidate changes the lines or the
evidence the decline names, or new evidence would make it Material.

## FO steps: review findings

Apply this checkpoint to findings from implementation, validation, detached audits,
consequential FO quick work and rejected gates.

1. Reviewers observe; workers' classifications and `actor:ensign` Resolutions are
   advisory. Preserve findings and assess the four evidence fields above, separating
   materiality, ownership and disposition. Missing required evidence or unresolved
   classification requires investigation or hold.
2. Within approved boundaries, FO may explicitly decline evidenced Deferred risk or
   Polish in the existing committed gate summary, naming the finding, reason, candidate
   revision and the lines or evidence it rests on. When that summary is already
   consumed, FO writes the decline under `### FO declines` in the task file, committed
   with `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, and the terminal gate
   lists each entry there. This FO-authored decision requires no live worker or reviewer
   rerun for acknowledgement; preserve worker reports and verdicts.
3. Repairs require worker investigation without candidate mutation, distinct FO
   `fix` authorization through the runtime's addressable-worker boundary, then
   independent validation. Without that authorization, hold.
4. Scope, value, threshold, tolerance, risk-acceptance and acceptance-criteria
   changes require the Captain. Material findings cannot use the record-only lane;
   hold/route-for-decision forbids repair and reviewer rerun.
5. A round is one verdict of an external reviewer of the delivery on the PR head (Codex
   on the PR, RoboRev or another); FO counts rounds and records the count in the
   committed gate summary. A reviewer that a listed extension covers is read the way its
   `EXTENSION.md` says (`## Extensions`). A finding assessed Material, or labelled P1 by
   the reviewer, blocks in every round: a reviewer P1 is fixed and revalidated, or
   waived by the Captain with the reason recorded (step 4). For an external reviewer
   that has no P1 label, its highest severity level counts as P1 (e.g. RoboRev). Rounds
   1 and 2 follow steps 1 to 4. From round 3 a finding that is neither does not start a
   repair cycle: FO declines it in the committed gate summary, naming the finding, and
   files it as a new backlog task with `spacedock new` whose body carries the finding
   and the decline reason, or names the backlog task that already holds it when a later
   round repeats it; it never enters an open task's Scope. The terminal gate lists each
   such task.

Rejection routing carries evidence, classifications, authorized dispositions and assignment
without re-triage.

Materiality and ownership are independent. Owned Material is eligible for an
FO-authorized fix; out-of-scope Material holds as Needs decision. Deferred risk
or Polish may use the recorded FO decline above within existing risk acceptance.

A Needs decision put to the Captain at a gate carries FO's recommendation. His
plain approval accepts that recommendation only when the gate question says so,
for example "approving accepts the recommendation for D2; say if you object".
Without that sentence a decision he did not address stays open: FO records its
handling as FO's reading, never as his ruling, and asks him.

A decision an accepted ADR already settles is not asked again: FO applies it and states it
in the gate summary as `Precedent: ADR <number> — 「<that ADR's Words line>」`, and the
Captain may reopen it. An ADR with no Words line is quoted by the decision sentence it
applies, as `Precedent: ADR <number> (no Words line) — 「<that sentence>」`. Authority, a gate approval, a merge, an outward-facing action, an
irreversible change and money are always asked, whatever an ADR says, and an ADR on one
of them is never a `Precedent:` line.

A Captain ruling is his reply to the question it settles, given after that question
was put. FO never records as his ruling: silence on a decision the question did not
state approval accepts, consent he gave earlier to a different question, or a choice
he raised but did not make. FO answers a question the Captain asks at a gate before
dispatching on it, and returns a choice he raised to him rather than to a worker.

When the Captain chooses differently from the recommendation, FO writes
`Override: recommended <option>; Captain chose <option>; area: <area>` in the gate
resolution reason, so later workers find past rulings with `git grep 'Override:'` in
the state checkout.

## Decision records

The implementation worker writes one ADR file per decision by its stage principles.
Validation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>`, which
requires every record the candidate added or changed, plus `--require <numbers>` for
each `ADR:` number the task's `## Number guards` reserves and any number the
implementation report names; exit 1 or a missing record returns through the existing
feedback route, and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.

## FO steps: decision records

A ruling settled at a gate, in a worker report, or mid-stage feedback — a rule about
the product, a constraint, or a direction later work must respect — is landed as an
ADR before the next gate is presented, at latest by the terminal approval. A ruling
that governs only this task's own work stays in the task. A design names an ADR
by its ruling and the file's short title, with no number; FO reserves the number when
it dispatches implementation (Number guards) and the implementation worker writes
`docs/adr/<reserved number>-<short-title>.md`. FO confirms the validation ADR lint
passes before presenting the gate. A deferred user-facing capability belongs on
the product's journey map, not here.

## Captain amendments

A change the Captain makes to what he has accepted, whether at a gate approval,
between gates or at a validation gate, is an amendment. A change he asks for
while the gate that would accept it is still open is not one: he calls `revise`; at a stage
with no `feedback-to` that dispatches a worker, that stage's worker reworks it; at a stage
whose gate has a `feedback-to`, the revision goes to that target and the stage's worker
re-reviews it; and at `backlog`, which dispatches no worker, FO revises the recorded outcome,
scope or budget, or asks the proposal's author to.

FO appends one entry per amendment to the task's `## Captain amendments` section and
changes nothing else in it. FO adds no words of its own and does not move or rewrite a criterion:

```
## Captain amendments

### Amendment 1 — <date>, <gate or chat>
Captain: 「<his words, verbatim>」 (where he said them)
Asked: <the question or proposal he answered, verbatim, or the commit holding it>
Supersedes: <acceptance-criterion ids, or none> <optional: "(no replacement: <why>)">
Design: <optional: the design paragraph it overrides>
```

`Asked:` is required when his words do not name what they settle, such as 「同意第三點」. FO
names the amendment in the next dispatch's checklist. That worker (implementation, the
repair worker on a feedback route, or the worker of the stage a task is sent back to)
moves each superseded criterion's block verbatim from `## Acceptance criteria` into its
entry under a `Superseded text:` line, writes any replacement as a new `**AC-N**` under
a fresh id that says "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and never reuses an id. A
superseded criterion and the design paragraph named by `Design:` are withdrawn; evidence
and the Captain's acceptance script follow `## Acceptance criteria` plus the entries.

Sending an approved task back to an earlier stage, such as a design redo a release
review asks for, is the Captain's decision and is recorded as an amendment whose
`Design:` names what is redone; FO then runs `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir>
--set <slug> status=<stage>`, and that stage's gate is approved again before the task
moves on.

`python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, run by implementation and
validation, prints each defect and exits 1; repair findings return through feedback. It cannot see a skipped record or
move, or FO's words in `Design:`.

## Affected documents

Implementation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/doc_impact.py <base> <candidate>`
and records, for each listed document, `updated` or `unaffected: <reason>` in its
stage report; validation reruns it at the candidate and checks every listed
document carries one. Make the update itself by the retained-document practices in
the package's `references/retained-documents.md`.

## Number guards

Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.
`python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py --help` lists the flags and rules R1 to R6;
`trunk:`, `migrations-path:` and `adr-path:` (default `docs/adr`) come from this README's frontmatter.

- **Applied.** `check` freezes a migration in a commit recorded `Applied at:` (R2).
  `Applied: none as of <sha>` records that
  nothing was pushed up to that commit; a validator that finds none of `Applied at:`,
  `Not applied:` or `Applied: none` reports the missing record to FO instead of
  re-checking deploys. A task with no `Migration:` line owes none of these.
- **Check.** `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py check --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --task <task file>`
  runs at implementation exit, at validation and, after `git -C <repo> fetch`, on the PR
  head before FO asks for merge. Exit 2 is a configuration error, which returns to FO
  as a hold.
- **POC.** A task whose recorded `profile` is `poc` adds, edits and deletes no migration
  file and reserves no number. A `FAIL R6` crosses the POC boundary
  (a schema change persists across sessions): the worker records
  `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` naming the path, and the task is not repaired in
  place.

## FO steps: number guards

- **Reserve.** Before an implementation

# Repository stage workers

## Adoption and introducing sync

Preserve an existing `.dev2/model-roster.json`; startup and ordinary sync do not
ask again or rewrite it. Ask only when the workflow frontmatter lists `paseo`
and the Codex provider is available. Otherwise ask nothing, write nothing and
retain README behavior. For eligible adoption or introducing sync without an
existing roster, display the complete [recommendation](model-roster-defaults.json)
and ask through the host's question UI:

> Stage workers: ideation Astra/high, implementation Sol/high, validation Astra/high,
> all Codex through Paseo. Save this shared repository choice or customize it?

Offer Accept and Customize. Preselection is not an answer. Cancel, empty response
or silence writes nothing, including no directory. Accept prepares the displayed
file; Customize collects each stage's exact tuple one at a time. Supported models
are `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-6.1-sol`, with explicit `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`,
`max` or `ultra` effort, provider `codex` and host `paseo`. Other choices return to FO.
Set `selected_from` to the selected package version and `decision` to the explicit
answer reference; these are caller-recorded provenance, not authenticated consent.
Show the complete three-row candidate in the existing configuration review before
committing `<code-root>/.dev2/model-roster.json` through the repository's normal
change path. Explicit later edits or deletion take that same reviewed path.
Choosing Paseo does not enable its extension or grant access.

## Stage launch or continuation

Before record checks and Spacedock build, run
`python3 <package>/scripts/model_roster.py resolve --code-root <absolute-code-worktree-root> --stage <stage>`.
For validation repeat `--author-record <path>` for every contributing implementation
and repair record of the candidate, including continuations. Use the bound code
checkout, never cwd or the split-root state checkout. `repair` resolves the
implementation row. The command reads a clean committed snapshot, validates all
three rows and emits JSON; it writes no settings, state or dispatches.

Exit 0 with `source=readme-default` means absent: retain today's README model and
host behavior without a question or fabricated effort. Exit 1 names invalid,
uncommitted, unreadable or unsupported present data: return it to FO; no fallback.
A committed deletion restores README behavior. Recommendations never update an
accepted snapshot. For configured settings use Paseo's existing Codex route; a
native route request returns to FO.

Keep `Model:` and add this header to the normal dispatch record, using resolver
values rather than copying the recommendation:

```text
Roster: source=repository; role=implementation; provider=codex; model=gpt-6.1-sol; effort=high; host=paseo; digest=sha256:DIGEST; commit=SHA
```

For absence use `Roster: absent; source README default`. For validation retain all
author references/tuples and `family` in the record and existing report/gate summary.
Sol and Astra share OpenAI provider lineage: `same-family: openai` is informational,
not a refusal or diversity claim. Missing/unknown author evidence is `unverified`.
The resolver understands these Roster headers and historical `Model: MODEL (Codex
via Paseo, thinking EFFORT;...)` headers; other formats remain unverified. Existing
names/folder/coverage/law checks remain due but do not prove roster consumption.

Preflight live provider/model/effort capability, listed extension eligibility,
workspace placement, permissions and existing worker identity before build.
Preserve generated prompt, identity and runtime fields. A non-null generated
model/effort conflicting with the tuple is a transport mismatch: return to FO,
never patch the envelope. Pass provider/model and `settings.thinkingOptionId`
beside those fields on the existing Paseo route. After successful build immediately
spawn, then save its handle; checks and narration precede build.

A continuation resolves again and records its source. Reuse only when its effective
tuple matches the existing worker; changed tuples return to FO for authorized
fresh handoff, without mutating or duplicating a running worker. Capacity, network
and uncertain launches use current manual recovery, without model substitution.
Keep requested settings separate from supported child runtime/turn evidence of
actual model, effort, root and preserved permissions; echo or worker assertion
alone is insufficient. Missing decisive evidence returns to FO.

FO and special roles retain current model floors, triggers and delivery duties,
including the Paseo worker-local commit and FO publication/review split. This
slice adds no personal store, capacity automation, new law, special-role hosting,
native adapter or additional provider.
.
